question.text: This man was the first prime minister of independent India. He delivered the "Tryst with Destiny" speech and was one of the pioneers of non-alignment.
question.clue: This man gave the "Tryst with Destiny" speech, and coined the term "non-aligned movement," a movement he founded with Nasser and Tito.

swap.leadin: Name these words from around the world that each contain the letter J pronounced in different ways.
swap.text: Shah Jahan in India had this massive building constructed as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz.
swap.clue: A Moonlight garden is across the river from this building, and this structure is surrounded by red sandstone on three sides.

question.leadin: This country became the first Muslim-majority democracy to be led by a woman when Benazir Bhutto led the PPP to victory in 1988 elections.
question.text: Name this country where Bhutto was assassinated in 2007 at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi.
question.clue: Following its independence, this country's southern border was demarcated by the Radcliffe Line.

swap.text: This emperor, the grandson of Akbar, was confined to Agra Fort by his son Aurangzeb when he fell ill in 1658. Name this ruler who constructed the Taj Mahal for his late wife Mumtaz Begam.
swap.clue: The Peacock Throne was built for this ruler, who ordered the construction of the Red Fort.

question.leadin: After Sambhaji, the founder of the Maratha Empire, refused to convert to Islam, this ruler brutally executed him.
question.text: Name this emperor who reinstated the jizya tax on non-muslims, the successor to his father Shah Jahan.
question.clue: This ruler was denounced in an "epistle of victory," or Zafarnama, written by Gobind Singh.

swap.text: Afonso de Albuquerque conquered this city on India's west coast in 1510. It remained a Portuguese possession until India annexed it in Operation Vijay.
swap.clue: Colony state, which was seized in Operation Vijay, is where Francis Xavier proselytized and is buried.

question.leadin: In a 1962 war, China fought for control of the Aksai Chin part of this region, which lies beyond the Line of Actual Control.
question.text: Name this northern region of the Indian subcontinent that lies west of the Himalayas. The Indian part of it is administered alongside Jammu.
question.clue: A conflict over this region was ended by the Tashkent Declaration following its invasion in Operation Gibraltar.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the cartoons of Thomas Nast.
swap.text: In order to attack Catholicism, Nast depicted an upside-down American flag, ruins of a public school, poor, defenseless protestant schoolchildren, and crocodiles with bishop hats for snouts on the banks of an "American" version of this river.
swap.clue: The iron-rich Magadha kingdom along this river's banks gave birth to a dynasty ruled by Nanda.

question.text: In this city, a "pact" between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League committed both to opposing the British Raj. Colin Campbell relieved a pre-Raj siege of this city during the Sepoy mutiny.
question.clue: This city's British Residency was besieged for several months in 1857.

swap.leadin: It was founded in 1906, and called for a religious integrated, independent India until 1940.
swap.text: Name this group which shifted positions in that year, working for the partitioned state that became Pakistan.
swap.clue: One of its leaders proposed the Fourteen Points in response to the proposals given in the Nehru Report.

question.text: This company operative led British troops to victory at the Battle of Plassey and served as the first British Governor-General of India.
question.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

swap.leadin: This empire's ruler Rajaraja the Great built the Brihadisvara temple, dedicated to Shiva.
swap.text: Rajaraja the Great ruled this empire which extended influence over much of the eastern Indian Ocean. Rajaraja and his successor Rajendra led this empire during its successful invasions of Sri Lanka and the Srivijaya kingdom.
swap.clue: The Maldives and the competing Pandya dynasty were conquered by Rajaraja I of this empire, who later built the Brihadisvara ] Temple.

question.leadin: These people's Pallava script was adapted into one of the earliest Javanese scripts, Kawi.
question.text: Name these people, whose king Rajendra I invaded the Srivijaya empire and Malaysia in the 11th century. At their height, these people were ruled by three kingdoms: the Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas.
question.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

swap.text: The Nizams once paid tribute to this empire that dominated the Deccan Plateau. Founded by Shivaji, it overtook the Mughals as a regional power and fought three wars with the British in the late 1700s.
swap.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

question.leadin: This organization is believed to have covertly owned a number of merchant ships known as the Sea Pigeons, which it used to smuggle weapons out of North Korea.
question.text: Name this terrorist organization, which had "air" and "sea" branches and was known for its use of suicide bombers in political assassinations, including that of Ranasinghe Premadasa in 1993.
question.answerHtml: Tamil Tigers [accept Liberation Tigers of Tamil Elam or LTTE]
question.clue: This group, based out of Kilinochchi, suffered its final defeat at Mullaitivu.

swap.text: The sudden appearance of a footed slab in Funan is evidence of South Asian spice trade, since slabs had been found in the Tissamaharama site in this region. The Mahavamsa details the arrival of Prince Vijaya to this region.
swap.clue: Failing irrigation tanks triggered the Great Famine in this country's Anuradhapura Kingdom, which fell to Chola invasions.

question.text: The famine also hit this historical region, where earlier events included the Battle of Seringapatam and British campaigns against Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan.
question.clue: This kingdom's last sultan successfully used rockets with attached blades in the Battle of Pollilur but died in 1799 while defending Seringapatam.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the Pindaris, a group of mounted marauders in India.
swap.text: The Pindaris were finally defeated by this first Governor General of India, who was impeached by Pitt the Younger.
swap.clue: One of his colleagues Elijah Impey was accused of impropriety by Nuncomar.

question.text: The Mysorean ruler Hyder Ali reprimanded his admiral, Ali Raja, for blinding the sultan of this place. Operation Cactus intervened in a much later coup attempt in this territory.
question.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a group of people comprised of 36 clans. FTPE.
swap.text: Claiming to be descendents of the original Kshatriya, these Hindu peoples held Northern India during the Middle Ages. Their dynasties included the Chauhan and Sisodias, and they were incorporated into the Mughal Empire as part of a marriage-based alliance with Akbar.
swap.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.
